parsed.rationale: Both `AsyncNotificationMessage` (in `Shared/Core/Sources/Core/Observation/AsyncMessage.swift`) and `MainActorNotificationMessage` (in `Shared/Core/Sources/Core/Observation/MainActorMessage.swift`) share 3 of 3 members structurally, with `shared_field_count: 3`. The only differing slot is the `sending` ownership annotation on `makeMessage`'s `Notification` parameter — `sending Notification` in `MainActorNotificationMessage` vs plain `Notification` in `AsyncNotificationMessage` — which reflects a concurrency-context specialisation, not a domain difference. The two shared members `name:Notification.Name` and `makeNotification:(_ message: Self, object: Subject?) -> Notification` are identical and belong in a common parent protocol `NotificationMessage` within the `Core` package. Each child protocol then refines `NotificationMessage` and declares only its own variant of `makeMessage`, keeping the `sending` annotation where it is semantically required.
